rationale: The evidence pack has no first-party benchmark dataset, WER methodology, or evaluation write-up backing AssemblyAI's accuracy claims. The docs only make accuracy assertions, such as Medical Mode improving terminology accuracy. Community threads report that commenters asked for WER benchmarks (LibriSpeech, TED) and found none, and that marketing claims like "world's most advanced" lacked supporting methodology. Those threads are old launch-era discussions, so current documentation may differ, which is why confidence is medium rather than high.

The evidence pack contains no first-party pricing documentation: no per-minute or per-hour rate, and no itemized prices for add-ons such as Medical Mode or diarization. Without published rates, an agent cannot compute a job's cost before submitting it. The community items mention pricing only vaguely ("on par with google", a volume-discount threshold) and do not supply computable published rates.

The public docs cover the full pre-recorded flow. The SDK "uploads, submits, and polls for you in a single call", and a synchronous HTTP endpoint returns transcripts for audio up to 20 minutes with no polling or webhooks. Probes confirm a machine-readable OpenAPI spec and llms.txt are live, and agent-specific instruction files are published, so an agent with a key can plausibly complete the job without a human. Missing for 10: explicit evidence of the API-key authentication scheme in the docs, and a hands-on or independent report of an agent completing submission-to-transcript end to end.

A probe confirms a live llms.txt at assemblyai.com/llms.txt (HTTP 200), and the docs also publish a /docs/llms.txt. Beyond that, AssemblyAI ships agent-oriented docs: an agent-instructions.md that agents can refetch via AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md or .cursorrules one-liners, with token-saving query parameters (?lang, ?excludeSpec). It also documents a coding-agent-prompts page with curated SDK context and a Docs MCP server for mid-session doc lookups. The probe-verified llms.txt is the independent corroboration, and the 404 on docs.md is minor given the other agent-facing surfaces.

It also offers an LLM Gateway that applies frontier reasoning models to transcripts, for example to generate structured meeting notes, so AI-generated insights from the user's audio data are a first-party capability. These are delivered via the API rather than a dashboard experience, and evidence is docs-only. missing for 10: evidence of in-product (UI/Playground) insight surfacing, explicit actionable suggestions beyond summaries and analysis, independent or hands-on corroboration of insight quality.
